Subject: Re: Removable Hard Drives

Even if you don't find a PATA to SATA converter, it's possible to just
purchase a PCI PATA controller (or PCI-E if your new stations use that) to
add PATA capability to your new systems, so that you could continue to hook
up the drives in the same manner as before

I've seen both PCI and PCI-E PATA controllers in the $20-25 range, which is
surely cheaper than new drives/caddies/bays, and probably close to same
price as any converter you'll find

Regards,

Chad Coller
Manager, ITS Help Desk

On 3/4/08 8:09 PM, "Jeff Tjiputra"  wrote:

> We have an IT Certification lab with removable hard drives.  We have about 50
> workstations with the removable hard drive shells on them.  We also have about
> 200 hard drives in the matching cases.  All of these are PATA drives.
> 
> We just upgraded the lab and now the new computers only have SATA controllers.
> 
> Have any of you came across a similar situation?  Is there a cheaper
> alternatives than just buying 200 new SATA drives along with the shells and
> cases?  Is there a SATA to PATA converter?  I've seen one going the other way,
> not sure about this one.
> 
> Thanks,
